In [[operator theory]], an area of mathematics, '''Douglas' lemma'''<ref name="Douglas1966">
{{cite journal
| last = Douglas
| first = R. G.
| title = On Majorization, Factorization, and Range Inclusion of Operators on Hilbert Space
| journal = Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
| volume = 17
| pages = 413&ndash;415
| year = 1966
| issue = 2
| doi = 10.2307/2035178
| jstor = 2035178
| mr = 203464
| doi-access = free
}}</ref> relates [[Matrix decomposition|factorization]], range inclusion, and majorization <!-- [[Majorization]] discusses a different topic, so is not currently appropriate to link to--> of [[Hilbert space]] operators. It is generally attributed to [[Ronald G. Douglas]], although Douglas acknowledges that aspects of the result may already have been known. The statement of the result is as follows:

'''Theorem''': If <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> are [[bounded operator]]s on a Hilbert space <math>H</math>, the following are equivalent:
# <math>\operatorname{range} A \subseteq \operatorname{range} B</math>
# <math>AA^* \leq \lambda^2 BB^*</math> for some <math>\lambda \geq 0</math>
# There exists a bounded operator <math>C</math> on <math>H</math> such that <math>A=BC</math>.
Moreover, if these equivalent conditions hold, then there is a unique operator <math>C</math> such that
* <math>\Vert C \Vert^2 = \inf \{\mu :\, AA^* \leq \mu BB^*\}</math>
* <math>\ker A = \ker C</math>
* <math>\operatorname{range} C \subseteq \overline {\operatorname{range} B^*}</math>.

A generalization of Douglas' lemma for unbounded operators on a Banach space was proved by Forough (2014).<ref name=FOR:14>{{cite journal
| last = Forough
| first = M.
| title = Majorization, range inclusion, and factorization for unbounded operators on Banach spaces
| journal = Linear Algebra and Its Applications
| volume = 449
| pages = 60&ndash;67
| year = 2014
| doi = 10.1016/j.laa.2014.02.033
| doi-access = free
| mr = 3191859
}}</ref>
